question: How many of the 3,708 multi-element genes the runtime's MEAN form cannot fit even at M2h's fixed scale 0.2146 -- `lane-residue`'s residue -- are FITTED (runnable and informative) under the MULTIPLICATIVE form of `lane-multrna`'s committed table, and how many under that same form with M2h's scale applied? A lookup: two identity matches and a runnability test that already exist. No RNA value is opened, nothing is fitted, and no form is proposed, because the form in question is already validated.
identity: The MATCH FIELD IS THE GENE SYMBOL, `combine2.GeneRules.symbol`, which is the `symbol` column of `lane-multrna`'s committed per-gene table (`data/results/multrna_result.json`, field `genes_table.columns`) and the same string `lane-residue` passed to `residue.gene_residue` as the gene's name. It is the only identity the two tables share: 7h's table also carries `gene` and `gene_id` (ENSG), but `lane-residue`'s committed per-gene table (`data/results/residue_genes.json`) carries NEITHER -- its rows hold only `chrom` and the distribution columns, with no gene identity at all. THAT IS WHY THE RESIDUE'S IDENTITIES ARE RE-DERIVED here rather than read (see RE_DERIVED), and why the re-derivation is reconciled against `lane-residue`'s committed counts as a check of this lane.
re_derived: The residue's 3,708 IDENTITIES are re-derived exactly as `lane-residue` derived its counts, by the same code on the same pinned programs: the 24 compiled non-coding programs are gated and parsed with `compile.gate_program` at `combine2.SELECTION`, the multi-element genes come from `combine2.multi_rule_genes` and `combine2.gene_rules`, a gene is ELIGIBLE when `combine2.classify` gives no reason, EXCLUDED when `combine2.fit('mean', rho)` fails with `basal_not_positive`, and in the RESIDUE when `combine2.fit('mean', scalefit.scaled_rho(rho))` fails the same way -- two calls to 7d's own fit per gene, never the identity q_scaled = SCALE * q. `lane-residue`'s committed Q1_counts are read AFTERWARDS and reconciled; a disagreement is a finding of this lane and not something to repair. The only thing this lane adds to that run is the gene's SYMBOL, which `lane-residue` computed and did not serialise.

count_definitions.count_1_committed_table: COUNT 1, 'fitted in the committed table': the residue symbols that appear in `multrna_result.json`'s `genes_table` rows. That table IS 7h's committed multiplicative population: the genes the multiplicative form made runnable and informative AND that passed 7h's RNA-table row checks, which is 16,509 of the 16,678 its census counts informative (169 fell to `population_exclusions.multiplicative`: 139 `gene_id_not_on_exactly_one_row_of_every_table` and 30 `symbol_not_on_exactly_one_gene_id`). ONLY THE `symbol` COLUMN OF THAT TABLE IS READ. Its `P` and `D` columns are predictions and RNA and are NOT opened, loaded or touched by this lane. Reported beside COUNT 1b, the same question asked PREDICTOR-SIDE ONLY -- `saturate.fit(rho).ok` and the closed form's range above INFORMATIVE_LOG2 across the thirteen reader cells, which is 7h's census definition of informative before any RNA table -- so that the row checks' 169 cannot be mistaken for a failure of the form.
count_definitions.count_2_at_the_scale: COUNT 2, 'fitted at 0.2146': the residue genes for which `saturate.fit(scalefit.scaled_rho(rho))` is ok and the multiplicative closed form's predicted log2 level is not the same in all thirteen reader cells (its range exceeds INFORMATIVE_LOG2) -- THE SAME runnability and informativeness test 7h's committed table used, applied to the scaled observations. `scaled_rho` is `scalefit`'s own: RHO_i -> 1 - SCALE * (1 - RHO_i), every element's effect multiplied by M2h's fixed scale, taken as a CONSTANT from `ac5580b` via `scalefit.SCALE`. NOTHING IS FITTED: the scale is not re-estimated, no level is chosen after seeing a count, and the multiplicative form has no parameter of its own (`saturate.FIT['nothing_fitted']`). The scale is M2h's MULTIPLICATIVE-form scale (`magcal_result.json`, `scales.multiplicative`), which is the form it is applied to here.
count_definitions.complement: THE COMPLEMENT: how many of the 3,708 are informative under NEITHER -- neither in 7h's committed table nor under the scaled multiplicative test -- reported with each gene's reason from `saturate.fit`, so that a count of genes the multiplicative form cannot run is never reported as a count of genes it fits. A gene is in the complement when it is in neither count.

implication_rule: Decided on the UNION of COUNT 1 and COUNT 2 as a share of the 3,708, with the threshold MOST = 0.5 fixed here before the match. ALREADY_ANSWERED, if the share exceeds 0.5: most of the residue is fitted multiplicatively, so THE RESIDUE IS THE ADDITIVE FORM'S STRUCTURAL FAILURE AND IS ALREADY ANSWERED BY THE FORM M2h VALIDATED, AND NO NEW FORM IS NEEDED. NOT_ANSWERED, if the share is 0.5 or below: most of the residue is not fitted multiplicatively either, which is reported and NOTHING IS PROPOSED. The threshold is the plain reading of the word: a majority is 'most'. Neither branch is a claim about expression: `multrna`'s own outcome on measured RNA was WORSE, which LIMITATIONS carries forward word for word, and a gene a fit can accept is not a gene the model predicts -- which `lane-recovered` (`f775e9b`) had to establish as a separate registration on separate data.
implication: ALREADY_ANSWERED: 3669 of the 3708 genes the runtime's mean form cannot fit even at M2h's fixed 0.2146 (98.9%) are fitted under the multiplicative form -- 3289 of them are in `lane-multrna`'s committed table and 3669 are runnable and informative under the same test with the scale applied -- so THE RESIDUE IS THE ADDITIVE FORM'S STRUCTURAL FAILURE AND IS ALREADY ANSWERED BY THE FORM M2h VALIDATED, AND NO NEW FORM IS NEEDED. 39 are informative under neither. No RNA value was opened and no test is registered here
why_the_scale_can_only_help: Stated in advance, from the algebra, so that neither count can be read as a surprise. The multiplicative form has no basal share to exhaust -- with every element removed the level is T*exp(-sum beta)/R0 > 0 -- so `basal_not_positive`, the reason the mean excludes all 12,500, CANNOT arise under it at all. Its only predictor-side refusals are `inhibitor_strength_above_1` (an inhibiting element with RHO_j > 1/(1 - H) = 2) and `exponent_beyond_float_range` (sum of -ln RHO_i above `saturate.EXPONENT_LIMIT` = 700). Multiplying every effect by SCALE = 0.2146 shrinks an inhibitor's lift, so the inhibitor bound becomes RHO_j <= 1 + 1/SCALE = 5.660, and shrinks every beta_i by more than the log does, so the exponent bound gets no harder. THEREFORE COUNT 2 CANNOT BE BELOW THE PREDICTOR-SIDE COUNT 1b, and the only genes either count can lose are the ones with a strong inhibitor. That is an arithmetic prediction, declared here before the count, and the run CHECKS it: `BOUND_CHECKS` below. ONE CAVEAT, stated rather than discovered: RUNNABILITY cannot be lost to the scale, but INFORMATIVENESS could be, because scaling shrinks every |log2 RHO_i| and so shrinks the closed form's range across the thirteen reader cells; a gene whose unscaled range was already within a factor 1/SCALE of INFORMATIVE_LOG2 = 1e-9 could fall below it. So the claim is exact for runnability and is a near-certainty, not a theorem, for informativeness. Every gene on which it fails is REPORTED, by name, and nothing is repaired.
bound_checks: Checked on every one of the 3,708, and a violation is reported, not repaired: (a) every residue gene refused by `saturate.fit` is refused for `inhibitor_strength_above_1` or `exponent_beyond_float_range` and NEVER for `basal_not_positive`, which the multiplicative form has no state for; (b) every gene runnable unscaled is runnable scaled, which is exact; (c) every gene informative unscaled is informative scaled, which is the near-certainty the caveat above names, so a failure is a named finding and not an error; (d) `combine2.fit('mean', rho)` fails `basal_not_positive` and `combine2.fit('mean', scaled_rho(rho))` fails it too, which is the residue's own definition, re-asserted per gene; (e) the mean form's q on the scaled observations equals SCALE times its q on the unscaled, the identity `lane-scalefit` proved and `lane-residue` re-checked.
multrna_census_sentence: of the 17,983 multi-element genes combine2.classify admits, the multiplicative composition makes 16,784 runnable (1,199 are not: 1199 inhibitor_strength_above_1) and 16,678 informative across the thirteen reader cells; 7d's forms made 4,779 (the runtime's mean) and 2,536 (promoter competition) informative, and 11,802 of the multiplicative form's informative genes are informative under neither 7d form (under the runtime's mean: 11396 basal_not_positive, 331 inhibitor_strength_above_1, 75 runnable_not_informative); 2,439 genes are informative under all three forms, before the RNA tables' row check
what_this_is_not: not a test, not a registration and not a claim about expression. Every count here is whether a fit accepts a gene, which is arithmetic on the elements' own removal observations. lane-multrna's outcome on measured RNA was WORSE and that is carried forward unchanged: the multiplicative form being the one that CAN RUN these genes is not the multiplicative form reading closer to measured RNA on them. NO RNA VALUE WAS OPENED IN THIS LANE
prior_exposure: What this lane had seen before it was written, stated so that no number here can be mistaken for a blind one. `lane-scalefit`'s and `lane-residue`'s counts (17,983 eligible, 12,500 excluded, 8,792 recovered, 3,708 in the residue; median top1 0.0888, max top1 0.210, n_eff 25.9, 0 recovered by a cap at L >= 0.25) are in the brief and in the commit messages `7f65544` and `5d2c8f5`. `lane-multrna`'s committed census sentence is in `multrna_census.json` and was read before this file was written: 16,784 of the 17,983 runnable multiplicatively, 16,678 informative, 11,802 of them informative under neither 7d form, of which 11,396 are `basal_not_positive` under the mean. THAT LAST NUMBER ALREADY BOUNDS THIS LOOKUP from one side and was known: the 3,708 are a subset of the 12,500 the mean excludes as `basal_not_positive`, and 11,396 of those 12,500 are informative multiplicatively, so at most 1,104 of the 3,708 can fail to be. The counts below are therefore NOT a surprise and are not reported as one; what they add is the exact figure per population and the scaled form's, neither of which is in the record. `saturate.WHY_NOT_SATURATING` and its 199-of-210 were read too. The IMPLICATION_RULE's threshold was fixed knowing all of this, which is why it is a plain majority and not a number chosen to be cleared.
limitations: A LOOKUP, not a test. Every number here is whether a fit accepts a gene, which is arithmetic on the elements' own removal observations. No RNA value was opened in this lane and no claim about expression is made or implied.

`lane-multrna`'s outcome on measured RNA was WORSE, carried forward word for word: the multiplicative form being the one that CAN RUN these genes is not the multiplicative form reading closer to measured RNA on them. Whether any of the 3,708 would read closer under it is a SEPARATE registration on separate data, as `lane-recovered` (`f775e9b`) had to be for the genes that recovered at the scale alone.

COUNT 1 is a membership test against a committed table, so it inherits that table's population exclusions: 169 of 7h's 16,678 informative genes are absent from it for RNA-table row reasons (139 `gene_id_not_on_exactly_one_row_of_every_table`, 30 `symbol_not_on_exactly_one_gene_id`) and not for anything about the form. COUNT 1b is the same question without those exclusions and is reported beside it.

The match is on the gene SYMBOL, which 7h itself found is not always one gene_id: its census counts 16,648 of the 16,678 informative genes whose symbol names exactly one. A residue symbol that names two gene_ids could match a 7h row that is not the same locus. The count of residue symbols that are not unique within this run is reported.

The residue identities are RE-DERIVED, not read, because `lane-residue`'s committed per-gene table carries no gene identity. The re-derivation is reconciled against its committed Q1_counts and a disagreement is reported as a finding.

M2h's scale is applied to the multiplicative form's observations as a fixed constant. That is what `magcal` fitted it for (`scales.multiplicative`), but it was fitted on 8,181 TRAINING genes, and nothing here establishes that it is the right magnitude for THIS population -- `lane-scalehet` holds the question of whether one global scale is even the right shape.

The multiplicative form keeps the bridge's exact-reproduction principle at the intact state (`saturate.FIT['principle']`); the SCALED form does not, exactly as `scalefit` recorded for the mean. A scaled element's run reproduces 0.2146 of its own removal observation, not the observation.
This lane registers no RNA test, proposes no form and changes no default. The runtime's `activator_combination` default is untouched.
money: none: no request is sent and no key is read

sources.accession: the 24 compiled non-coding programs 7d, 7h and lane-residue ran
reader v1 ENCODE DNase-seq narrowPeak files, 13 biosamples

exclusions: 7d's own: one rule, rules in several programs, a measured rule, an unreadable or exactly-1 observation, an action that disagrees with it, no activating rule
genes the mean form excluded for a reason other than basal_not_positive are not in this lookup's population at all
genes the mean form recovered at M2h's scale are counted and then dropped: the population is the residue alone
COUNT 1 inherits 7h's table's own RNA-row exclusions (139 + 30); COUNT 1b is the same question without them

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 0099d10

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
